title: Bipartite matching is in BPP
statement: The language of encodings of bipartite graphs that have a perfect matching belongs to BPP under the given verifier model. Explicitly, there are a Boolean verifier $M$ and natural numbers $a,k$ such that the verifier is efficient according to that model, and for every input word $x$, if $x$ is in the language then a uniformly random string of $a(|x|+1)^k$ bits makes $M$ accept with probability at least $2/3$; if $x$ is not in the language, such a random string makes $M$ reject with probability at least $2/3$.
hypotheses_covered: The language is the set of encodings of bipartite graphs with a perfect matching
There exist a Boolean verifier and natural numbers $a,k$
The verifier satisfies the efficiency predicate of the polynomial-time verifier model
For every input word in the language, acceptance probability is at least $2/3$ using $a(|x|+1)^k$ random bits
For every input word outside the language, rejection probability is at least $2/3$ using $a(|x|+1)^k$ random bits
